questions.question: Explain four reasons for the location of settlements in South Africa, with examples.
questions.expected_answer: Water is the most important, so towns grew beside rivers and springs, such as Vereeniging on the Vaal and Bloemfontein around a spring. A good climate, rainfall and vegetation attracted farmers, so more people live in the wetter east. Resources and activities created towns, such as Kimberley for diamonds, Johannesburg for gold, west coast fishing towns and ports such as Durban. Laws under apartheid, such as the Group Areas Act, forced people into certain areas, as at District Six.

questions.question: Describe the world's population distribution and explain why Cairo grew where it is.
questions.expected_answer: The world's more than eight billion people are spread unevenly: about six in ten live in Asia, and crowded regions include South and East Asia, Europe, the north-east United States, West Africa and the Nile valley, while deserts, cold lands, rainforests and mountains are nearly empty. Cairo, Egypt's capital, grew on the Nile where the valley meets the delta because the river gave water in the desert, fertile soil and transport, its position helped trade, and it has been a capital for over a thousand years.

questions.question: Describe three modern medical discoveries and the people responsible.
questions.expected_answer: In 1796, Edward Jenner used cowpox from a milkmaid to protect James Phipps from smallpox, creating the first vaccine; smallpox was eradicated in 1980. Louis Pasteur proved that germs cause decay and disease with his swan-neck flask, invented pasteurisation and made vaccines from weakened germs, and Robert Koch found the TB germ in 1882. In December 1967, Christiaan Barnard's team at Groote Schuur Hospital performed the world's first human heart transplant.
